journey.title: Escape closes only the innermost open submenu
journey.goal: Escape in the Facts submenu returns to Facts while the About submenu stays open

functionalJourney.title: Open nested submenus with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: About and Facts submenus open on click

guards.title: Escape in a first-level submenu returns to the menubar
guards.goal: Escape in the About submenu closes it and focuses About

plan.root_cause: When pressing Escape in a submenu, the code incorrectly closed all open submenus of the root menu (via this.elements.rootMenu.closeChildren()) instead of only closing the current submenu. This caused the parent submenu (About) to close unexpectedly and focus to move to the parent menubar item (About) rather than remaining in the parent submenu's menu item (Facts).
plan.repair_strategy: Replace the Escape key handler in non-top-level menus to close the current submenu via its toggle (which also focuses the parent menu item) instead of closing all submenus of the root menu.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Escape in the Facts submenu will close only the Facts submenu, move focus to the Facts item, and leave the About submenu open.
functional_risks: Altering the Escape key behavior in submenus might affect other keyboard navigation patterns if the toggle.close() method has unintended side effects.
If the parent menu item does not have a toggle (should not happen for a submenu item), the Escape key would have no effect, potentially trapping focus.
verification_requirements: After the fix, the journey step 5 (Escape in Facts submenu) should pass: focus on #facts, aria-expanded of #facts false, aria-expanded of #about true.
Verify that Escape in other submenus (e.g., if there were a deeper level) behaves correctly.
Verify that Escape in the menubar (when no submenu is open) still closes the menubar controller if open, and that Escape in a menubar item with no submenu does nothing (or as per pattern).
